content:
maria: Heads-up — canary rollout for release v2.9.1 just triggered a p95 spike on runtime nodes in us-west-2. Alert from oncall-bot below.
oncall-bot: Canary alert: p95 latency crossed 1200ms for route /api/generate on canary pool cw-canary-7 (threshold 900ms).

maria: Seeing the same in dashboards, looks correlated with the kernel allocator tweak merged in runtime yesterday (commit a3f2b9c).

kenji: I can bisect but need a quick repro. Can someone capture a short profile of the canary traffic? Prefer flamegraph + kv cache metrics.

liam: Kicked off a 5m sampling run on the canary group: https://perf.internal/redwood/canary/171823 - includes pprof snapshots.

ana: quick note — traffic mix on canary is skewed to long-seq (avg seq 640) tonight due to a partner test. That could amplify allocator pressure.

maria: Thanks @ana. Two options I see: (1) Rollback the allocator change from canary immediately, (2) throttle canary qps to reduce tail latency while we bisect, or (3) fallback route to rwd-7b-compat model variant. Thoughts?

kenji: Prefer rollback if we can do it fast. Bisect will take >30m. Rollback command: `kubectl set image deploy/runtime=runtime:stable-a3f2b9c --record` (ops already prepared).

liam: Ops runbook suggests throttle first if user-facing impact is low. Do we know affected % of requests failing SLO?

maria: From SLO monitor ~8% of requests in canary window exceeded p95 target, error rates are stable. Partner tests are non-prod but they exercise production latency.

ana: If we throttle, we should also switch routing policy to fall back to rwd-7b for sequences >512. That's a quick config flip: `route-policies set --canary --max-seq 512 --fallback rwd-7b-compat`

oncall-bot: Ops note: Autoscaler cooldown 300s, rolling image update will affect ~12 pods, expected <5m to complete once initiated.

sachin: I'm +1 for rollback. We don't want customer-visible regression even if it's partner traffic. :thumbsup:

liam: I'm leaning toward throttle + routing change to buy time for bisect so we don't rollback changes that may have other perf upsides. :thinking_face:

maria: Ok decision call: rollback now. Rationale: clear p95 breach, partner tests still count as canary signal, rollback is fast and safe. We'll reopen canary after bisect.

maria: @ops-team please run the rollback command now (prepare a quick postmortem of the bisect after).

kenji: On it. Starting rollback: `kubectl set image deploy/runtime=runtime:stable-a3f2b9c --record`

oncall-bot: Deploy started at 1718234805, updating 12 pods.

liam: Post-rollback note — once stable, let's run targeted runs of `./scripts/run_bench.sh --model rwd-13b --seq 512 --qps 60 --profile` and the kv-cache profiling job to reproduce locally.

maria: Agreed. Assigning follow-ups: kenji (bisect & flamegraphs), liam (bench repro & perf tests), ana (route policy verification), sachin (postmortem draft). I'll open a short ticket.

sachin: Will draft postmortem, flagging that we should add a canary filter for partner test traffic in future to avoid noisy signals.

oncall-bot: Deploy succeeded at 1718234920, average p95 returned to 430ms on canary within 90s.

maria: Verified in dashboards — p95 back to baseline. Thanks everyone. We'll keep the canary paused until bisect yields a fix or we have mitigations.

liam: Quick command for repro for anyone:```
./scripts/run_bench.sh --model rwd-13b --seq 640 --qps 20 --duration 300 
# collect with pprof: curl http://canary-pod:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=30 > canary.prof
```

kenji: I'll post bisect updates in this thread. Next update in ~40m.

maria: Closing the incident for now; reopen if regressions reappear. :white_check_mark:
